entries.summary: AuthN substrate Phase 4 — per-tenant MFA policy + 7-day grace + enforcement on sensitive endpoints (BE-4.1..4.5). Default policy stays 'off'; dev + test flows unchanged on the demo tenant.
entries.worktree: ../tms-authn (branch authn-feature) — D-03 isolation, main checkout untouched

new_files: backend/app/services/mfa_policy_service.py — reads/writes tenant_setting[key='mfa_policy']. Payload {mode: off|optional|required_for_sensitive_roles|required_for_all, grace_days: 7, activated_at: iso}. get_policy() returns well-formed defaults for any tenant. set_policy() stamps activated_at when flipping from off; preserves it when tightening (sensitive->all); clears it on flip-to-off (next flip-on restarts grace). is_mfa_required(session, tenant, roles, now=None) handles grace arithmetic + sensitive-role matching. required_by() returns the ISO deadline for the nag banner (None when policy is off/optional/role-exempt). SENSITIVE_ROLES = {CFO, HEAD_OF_TREASURY, ADMIN, COMPLIANCE_OFFICER}.

backend/tests/test_mfa_policy.py — 19 tests: policy defaults, activated_at stamping/preservation/clearing, is_mfa_required across every mode + grace window + role, required_by() nag deadline, /deals/{id}/approve enforcement toggle (default-off unchanged / policy-on refused / after /auth/mfa/consume allowed), /auth/me surfaces (mfa.policy_mode + mfa.required_by + mfa.passed_this_session + mfa.enrolled).
changed: backend/app/api/deps.py — require_mfa() rewritten as policy-aware. Reads mfa_policy_service.is_mfa_required(ctx.session, caller.tenant_id, caller.roles) at request time. When the policy says MFA is NOT required for this caller, the dep is a no-op. When it IS required, refuses with 403 MFA_REQUIRED unless caller.mfa_passed is True. Default-off policy means endpoints wearing require_mfa behave identically to pre-Phase-4 on the demo tenant.

backend/app/api/auth.py — GET /auth/me now (a) uses ctx.session instead of a fresh SessionLocal (fixes a worktree/test bug the old code hid behind a prod treasury.db), and (b) adds an 'mfa' block to the response: {enrolled, verified_at, passed_this_session, required_by, policy_mode}. The required_by field is the ISO deadline the client reads for the nag banner.

backend/tests/test_mfa_consume.py — Phase 3 tripwire test ('no endpoint wears require_mfa yet') replaced with a precise allow-list test ('require_mfa is wired to exactly these 2 endpoints') that fails loudly on any drift. Three Phase 3 tests updated for new policy-aware semantics (policy-off = allowed; policy-on + grace-elapsed + mfa_passed=false = refused).

done_when_verification.phase_4_done_when: Flipping the demo tenant to required_for_all makes /deals/{id}/approve return 403 MFA_REQUIRED for an unenrolled user; flipping back to off restores today's behaviour exactly.
done_when_verification.verified: test_approve_deal_refuses_without_mfa_when_policy_on exercises exactly that round-trip (set policy, collapse grace, expect 403; flip off, expect business logic to run). test_approve_deal_default_off_unchanged proves the pre-flip baseline. test_approve_deal_allowed_after_mfa_consume proves the enroll->verify->consume path produces a bearer that satisfies require_mfa even under enforce-all.

reversibility: Policy default is 'off'. A tenant that never calls set_policy() sees exactly today's behaviour on every endpoint — including the two now wearing require_mfa.
Flipping policy to 'off' is a one-call revert; activated_at clears so a later flip-on restarts the 7-day grace.
Removing the require_mfa dep from a specific endpoint is a one-line change (deals.py or admin_users.py).

entries.parked_check: Confirmed — Phase 4 touches no file/symbol/route forbidden by PARKED_PLANS.json. tenant_setting is the general-purpose per-tenant store added in S2 — new 'mfa_policy' key is additive.
operational_followups: Admin UI tab for policy mode is deferred to Phase 5 (backend) + a frontend FE-x task. No way to flip the policy from the UI today — only via direct DB writes or a future admin endpoint.
Phase 5 (BE-5.1..5.5) adds the admin endpoints that write mfa_policy with the four-eye pattern (ADR-0015), plus /admin/mfa/status (per-user enrollment table), plus audit_event per policy change.
